topic: Three-person resource reservations with access and capacity rules
basis: An explicitly authored mathematical development domain. These are supplied rules, not measurements of a real system. Produce a reusable finite-v0 theory; the local engine will check and plan independently.

interfaces.reservations.Actor: Type: enum with exactly alice, bob, carol.
interfaces.reservations.State: Type: plain record of exactly six bool fields alice_access, bob_access, carol_access, alice_reserved, bob_reserved, carol_reserved. Keep all 64 combinations in the carrier; validity is a separate predicate.
interfaces.reservations.capacity: Function with no parameters, integer return type 1..3, initially returns 1.
interfaces.reservations.occupied: Function params {state: reservations.State}, returns integer 0..3: number of reserved fields that are true. Convert each bool to 0 or 1 using an if; arithmetic operators take exactly two arguments.
interfaces.reservations.has_access: Function params {state: reservations.State, actor: reservations.Actor}, returns bool: selected actor's access field.
interfaces.reservations.is_reserved: Function params {state: reservations.State, actor: reservations.Actor}, returns bool: selected actor's reserved field.
interfaces.reservations.valid: Function params {state: reservations.State}, returns bool: each reserved actor has access AND occupied(state) <= capacity(). This must call the capacity function rather than hardcode 1.
interfaces.reservations.can_reserve: Function params {state: reservations.State, actor: reservations.Actor}, returns bool: valid(state) AND actor has access AND actor is not reserved AND occupied(state) < capacity().
interfaces.reservations.grant: Transition with state reservations.State and parameters reservations.Actor. Legal exactly when valid(state) AND selected actor lacks access. Set only that actor's access field to true.
interfaces.reservations.revoke: Transition with the same state and parameters. Legal exactly when valid(state) AND actor has access AND actor is not reserved. Set only that actor's access field to false.
interfaces.reservations.reserve: Transition with the same state and parameters. Legal exactly when can_reserve(state, action). Set only that actor's reserved field to true.
interfaces.reservations.release: Transition with the same state and parameters. Legal exactly when valid(state) AND actor is reserved. Set only that actor's reserved field to false; preserve access.
interfaces.reservations.two_reserved: Goal over reservations.State: valid(state) AND occupied(state) >= 2.
interfaces.reservations.three_reserved: Goal over reservations.State: valid(state) AND occupied(state) == 3.
interfaces.reservations.capacity_assumption: Assertion with no params: capacity() == 1. This assertion must be revised when the capacity assumption changes.
interfaces.reservations.valid_capacity: Assertion params {state: reservations.State}: valid(state) implies occupied(state) <= capacity(). Express implication as not antecedent OR consequent.
interfaces.reservations.reserve_requires_access: Assertion params {state: reservations.State, actor: reservations.Actor}: can_reserve(state, actor) implies has_access(state, actor).

requirements: Use precisely the named interfaces. Do not omit transitions, goals, or assertions. This task requires no additional helper declarations.
All predicates are total, including on invalid state combinations. Every transition is illegal on an invalid state. Do not silently repair invalid input states.
The transition parameter is an actor enum directly, not a record containing an actor. Functions use the parameter names shown above. Transition expressions bind state and action.
Enums are not tagged sums: select actor fields with nested if/equality expressions. Enum string literals need an explicit enum type annotation.
Keep the state type independent of capacity; capacity is a replaceable function used by the validity and reservation predicates.
Do not add external tools, host code, proof source, or empirical evidence. Supply candidate declarations with an honest provider-statement summary.
